body:
Reviewed the changes in this PR. This is primarily an internal code refactoring that reorganizes the Python codebase structure (moving files from `continuedev/libs/` to `continuedev/core/`) and updates the VS Code extension metadata.

The PR already includes appropriate documentation updates:
- VS Code extension README was updated to reflect the new positioning
- Package.json metadata was updated with correct links and descriptions
- License file was updated to Apache 2.0

No additional documentation changes are needed as this refactoring doesn't introduce new user-facing features or change existing APIs.

author: lun-4

body:
> > My idea on this is something like "model roles."
> 
> I didn't understand the separation between small/medium/large, but "summarizer" is a good role already for something like GPT-3.5. Could you elaborate on what `custom` would mean on that example?

Small/medium/large just meaning larger/slower vs. smaller/faster models. Seemed a bit more general than "summarizer", because gpt35 can be used for other tasks as well. Custom should exist because for example the small/medium/large/default might not be enough slots for all the LLMs someone wants, or at least it could be limiting. Or let's say they have their own super specific LLM that is used in a custom Step they've written. Then they'd want to be able to reference it with `sdk.models.custom["my_custom_model_name"]`.

body:
> > the small/medium/large/default might not be enough slots for all the LLMs someone wants, or at least it could be limiting.
> 
> I don't understand how would a custom model be used from the perspective of the code that already wants `models.large`, I can understand mapping for a custom Step, but that reads as if it's a separate example than the first sentence. If the intention was just to provide custom Step support, that's fine, and I apologize for misunderstanding.

No worries—I think there's a good point here: you can still get custom LLMs that aren't in sdk.models.small/medium/large/default by just importing it yourself into a custom step. So let's remove the `custom` thing in `Models`, but keep small/medium/large:

```python
config = ContinueConfig(
...
  models: Models(
    default=OpenAI("gpt4",...),
    small=OpenAI("gpt-3.5",...),
    large=None,  # This would fall back to the default model (these are all optional kwargs, except default)
  )
)
```

body:
@ishaan-jaff Cool stuff! My biggest concerns here are:

a) litellm depends on openai[datalib], which includes numpy and pandas, and would significantly increase our build size
b) making a single class for all of these providers would lead to a slightly less homogeneous experience in the Continue config file. We would still need a different class for connecting to local models or other custom models not supported by litellm, so this would cause most of these commercial providers to be in a single class, while other more specific providers (e.g. Ollama) would have their own unique class. This also means that litellm wouldn't completely remove the need for our LLM class to be implemented in a few separate files.

The solution I'm leaning toward is a "docs integration." We could give an example of how to use litellm [here](https://continue.dev/docs/customization), and allow users to use litellm, but without including it in the builtin library.

Open to your thoughts here, and really do appreciate what you've suggested.
author: sestinj

> The solution I'm leaning toward is a "docs integration." We could give an example of how to use litellm [here](https://continue.dev/docs/customization), and allow users to use litellm, but without including it in the builtin library.

body: Is there a quick step-by-step of what needs to be run locally to test out the plugin? I found the `runIde` task, but the plugin doesn't work, presumably some set of other things, related to the react app / extension aren't present yet?
author: bdruth

body:
@bdruth there is not, but this is something I should add. You can do roughly the following:

1. Steps 1 and 2 from here: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#environment-setup (if you're opening it from within JetBrains obviously the VS Code tasks won't work, so looking at the .vscode/tasks.json file and just running the commands one-by-one might be necessary). This step should carry out the building of the react-app, which will also automatically copy it over to the intellij-extension folder as needed
2. In JetBrains, after opening with the continue repo as the root of the workspace, there should be gradle tasks for building the plugin and "Run Plugin". If you build first, and then run, it should open up a new window where the plugin will start. In that new window, Continue will exist on the right side toolbar
3. It will attempt to download the server binary, but this has only been tested a limited amount. If that succeeds, it should work.

body:
@sestinj 

I have a little issue; maybe you can help.

When the `install_from_source.py` script runs the line `resp = run("cd ../../../server; poetry install; poetry run typegen")`, ~~declaration~~ files are created. This causes the `npm run build` command in the `continue/gui/` directory to fail when it tries to execute the `tsc` command.

https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/f3d1ef79be90335c742fd3e505fd1bfe40b9f402/gui/package.json#L7

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[install_from_source.py] -->|poetry run typegen| B(prepackage.js)
    B -->|npm run build| C(continue/gui/package.json)
    C -->|tsc| Error
```


How can I solve this?
author: LangLangBart

body: forced-pushed to rebase with `main`
author: LangLangBart

body:
I believe this is the issue: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/f3d1ef79be90335c742fd3e505fd1bfe40b9f402/server/continuedev/core/main.py#L105

I changed it to `Any` instead of `Step` because there was a circular imports dependency, which forced me to use a "fake" Step class. But then this later caused the problem that when a Pydantic class was being initialized, it would make a copy of the real `Step` object that I passed in, causing big issues

But this would be why the "unknown" type error is coming up

body:
@djcopley this is awesome! I think a Docker container would have huge benefit to Continue users and make setup much easier, something that we deeply care about. I'd actually love to hear more about some of the potential troubles that led to creating this, and what you are looking for in a reproducible setup.

To be quite honest about the PR: Many users will want to deploy in ways other than with Ollama, making this a bit of an unfair endorsement. But more importantly, anything we add to this repository requires responsibility, and though it's just one file, a Dockerfile would be an extreme focal point. As much as we might state otherwise, it would be treated as a product, one that comes with troubleshooting, security concerns, and lots of maintenance. For this reason, it's something we want to _really_, _really_ get right, and are actively working toward. Until then, it wouldn't be right to host this.

But what we can do is:
1. Help make setup as easy as possible for you! Docker containers are a great way to do this and if you could use our help getting one going we're more than happy to assist
2. Kickstart a conversation—what are the needs you have when setting up Continue, what guarantees would you want out of a setup process, how might we test those? This would be a great way to help us move toward the version that we _will_ maintain, and you'll probably come out of it having shaped an even better version of Continue : )
author: sestinj

body:
nice to see this is being worked on, it will make continue a true replacement for copilot

I've been using Copilot for a couple hundred hours, I found that important regarding autocompletion:
* word level autocompletion is very important (copilot does that with ctrl + arrow right)
* the amount of completion output should be configurable (as in lines or characters or guidance)
* the context given to the llm should have options to configure
 - when working with web projects (PHP for example) and SQL then the table schema in context is extremely helpful to the LLM, copilot currently is not doing that (JB phpstorm) so it only learns from available examples in context and hallucinates a lot
 - it would be nice if the data that is sent to the llm is viewable to the user (as debug/insight)
 - context should be configurable per section (as in how many tokens before, after cursor, how many of SQL, file structure, etc
 - copilot appears to have a "recently edited" temporary section it has in context, so if you worked in 3 tabs, lines from those areas are available for completion (at least for chat, not sure about autocompletion)
 
Performance
Depending on the model provider there would be massive performance improvements possible.
For example if you have a context of 5000 tokens, once they are processed they could be loaded from a KV cache again, that would save to reprocess everything, only new tokens from the end would need to be evaluated. 
Once the context window runs out a re-rope would allow to continue, that's magnitudes faster than a re-evaluation.
Any local running llm would allow to do that.

author: sestinj

body:
> @cmp-nct thanks for this, definitely a few new ideas here for me. Brief response to your bullets in order:
> 
> * we will do this! Turns out it's built into VS Code
> * planning on giving access to stop words and max tokens, which will allow you to "only complete single lines" if you'd like among other things
> * agreed
> * maybe we even go as far as allowing "plugins". lots to build, but could be very very useful for devs to define links between files themselves
> * agreed
> * not totally sure what each of these mean, but the pattern here is I'm very pro-configuration : )
> * recently edited, copy buffer, open tabs all will be taken into account
> 
> Your performance notes are very important—for this reason we'll probably be highly encouraging specific providers that we form-fit at first

Great to hear :)
I don't want to flood you with details, it's overwhelming. Just can't help but share the most concerning things I noticed, missed or found important. Maybe some of those resonate:)

Regarding 'context should be configurable per section (as in how many tokens before, after cursor, how many of SQL, file structure, etc':
What I meant is that the amount of data sent to the llm as "context" should have a broad configuration range, if possible fine tuned on the type of context.
I'm sure you have plenty of own ideas in that regard, for me I see 3 main areas:
1) The primary context - that's N lines of code BEFORE the cursor 
2) The post cursor context - that's if "fill-in" type is allowed. Basically any smart instruction-llm can do fill in with a good prompt but pure completion llms would need a fine tune for it. - so that's N lines of code AFTER the cursor
3) Metadata that is not in the direct flow of the context but important for completions:
 - Copilot always sends the function/class prototype to the llm for example, some functions/classes are too large to fit into context, but the prototype (arguments, return, possibly documentation) is especially important
 - SQL schemas (for example if a table is being used, if the schema is available that could be added as a "comment" in begin of llm prompt/context
  - filename of the file, possibly the project structure, possibly imports/includes (file header)
  - Copilot has recently improved a lot and one of those improvements seem to be the addition of "recently changed lines". So if I change 5 lines in 5 places in 3 files (total 25 lines added/changed) and then I go to file 4, copilot will sent those 25 changed lines in some form of "metadata" alongside the main completion request. 
  - And maybe a freeform text that can be added to context. Like the current continue.dev Chat feature, where you select lines and add them into context of the question. The same could be used for autocompletion maybe. So if you work on file_a.c and all the API is in file_b.c then maybe file_b.h could be added into context manually.

So what I meant is that those sections/subsections - if they are included - should have some configuration options in how much of them is sent to the LLM.
One of your primary difficulties for auto completion is the wide range of models and APIs available and the wide range of inference hardware and configuration options.
So depending on that some type of requests will need small context, some will need a lot, some will work well with metadata, some not.  The more we can configure, the more models and platforms will work well.

The idea of plugins is very interesting too.

I will stay tuned on the upcoming releases, very promising work
For the start I'd guess a minimal version will be fine, just wanted to share some ideas
author: cmp-nct

body:
Here goes the merge! This is still a beta version of tab-autocomplete, and should be understood as such, meaning please share your feedback! The best places to do this are the #feedback channel on Discord, GitHub Issues, or on the [Contribution Ideas Board](https://github.com/orgs/continuedev/projects/2?pane=issue&itemId=37654703) if you have thoughts on how to improve or would like to contribute code.

Over the next few weeks we will be focusing *a lot* on this feature, so expect significant improvement.

It will use `deepseek-coder:1.3b-base` on Ollama by default and we recommend this for now. If you'd really like to play around with the settings however, you can learn how to do this [here](https://continue.dev/docs/walkthroughs/tab-autocomplete). If there's some option you want and don't see, let us know! The goal is to make Continue's autocomplete *entirely configurable*.

body:
I'd like to add a request for an optional "idle time" parameter to the config. In the preview build, the autocomplete triggers on every change, resulting in continue.dev calling my local LLM multiple times per second and reprocessing the context each time. Usually it's not a problem because of smart context shift, but sometimes it decides to reprocess the entire context, resulting in some slowdown. I'd like to see an option where autocomplete only fires off if I pause typing for some configurable time period.
Thanks for your work and consideration of this request!

body:
@elabbarw Thanks for this thoughtful PR! My first thought is that a pattern is emerging in seeing a few attempts at authentication. There are going to be a ton of different providers, all with their own form of authentication, and as you've seen here with JetBrains not working, the requirement to download an entirely new NPM package, and the complication of extra parameters...it will add up to a lot of complexity for both users and maintainers.

With this in mind, we're hoping to do authentication once and do it really right (possibly a single point of auth for Continue, or at least something that doesn't require multiple different client-side auth providers). My preferred way of moving forward would be to revisit this in the near future when we start to build such "beyond the extension" features. But as we're designing this, it would be extremely helpful to understand what requirements led to this PR. Hopefully we can get all of them resolved in a more well-packaged product soon.

sestinj

body:
> @my8bit Thanks for doing this, I think it's a great addition. Out of extreme caution I think it would be best to remove engines -> node from the package.json at the root of `extensions/vscode`, reason being that they don't make it clear in their [documentation](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/extension-manifest#:~:text=The%20publisher%20name-,engines,-Y) whether this is used to determine whether an extension is incompatible. It would be unfortunate if this caused anyone on older node versions to be unable to download the extension.
> 
> And with strict mode, I'd say if an `npm i` succeeds now with strict mode, no changes necessary, then this can only help
> 
> Otherwise I think this looks ready to merge

This is a very good point about the version compatibility with VSCode itself. I researched it here a bit and here is what I discovered:
- The VSCode itself is using the `>=18.15.x and <19` and `18.17.1` from the main branch to be more specific
source: [docs](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#prerequisites), [.nvmrc](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/.nvmrc)
- My Windows version of the VSCode is using the `18.15.0`. You can check your from VSCode itself by opening `Help -> About`
- At the same time correct code contains the GitHub Actions that use the Node.js version v19.0.0. Theoretically, in setup without change from this, MR allows bundling the version of the extension that uses the incompatible syntax from Node.js v19.0.0 that will not work in the VSCode, that uses v18.15.0. In this case, the code will pass locally and will pass the CI job. Moreover, v19 is not officially supported by VSCode as stated in the docs above. Therefore I configured the pipeline files to use the Node.js version from the `.nvmrc` from the repo.
- When I started to dive into the issue from the description I realized that it's most probably the local inconsistency but that I do have. I checked the clean installation with v18.15.0 and it worked well for me.

IMHO the safest option is to stick to v18.15.0 (or `v18.17.1` or broad version in range `>=18.15.x and <19`) in `.nvmrc` and have a centralized and explicit version of the Node.js used across the project locally and on CI.

P.S. I found the issues with  `./install-dependencies.sh` as well, which I'm going to address in another PR.

body: @ashokgelal thanks for the PR! I want to make sure I understand how Msty works before merging: is it using Ollama under the hood, or does it just match its API format? Any reason why not OpenAI? And I assume from the code here that 10000 is the default port?
author: sestinj

body:
It is using Ollama under the hood but maintain its own version (we check compatibility issue with the models we support, for an example) and it is also very opaque to users, if you will, as the don't have to worry about installing Ollama as we'll do that for them.
Not OpenAI because we do support local models (not sure if I interpreted your question about that correctly). 

10000 is the default port but if that port is reserved by some other apps, then Msty pickup next available port.
author: ashokgelal

body:
@ashokgelal all makes sense! With the OpenAI question I was just wondering why not use the OpenAI API format, since it seems most people are moving toward that, including Ollama.

> @Iamshankhadeep I finally got around to testing this locally. Everything looks perfect, including the packaging with esbuild (you solved this very cleanly!). But it seems that VS Code isn't doing well with worker threads. In debugging mode, the worker never responds (can verify this by placing a breakpoint in the on message function).
> 
> Then when I packaged the extension and installed it as a .vsix, everything seemed to work fine, until using the @ codebase context provider causes the extension host to crash.
> 
> Had you seen the same issue or have any ideas? [microsoft/vscode#88386](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/88386) seems like the most closely related issue, though seemed to have been solved

I was having the same issue while testing on this `worker_thread` but terminating the  worker thread `worker.terminate();` seems to fix that.

>until using the @ codebase context provider causes the extension host to crash.

I can think of one issue probably using @ codebase opening too many worker threads before terminating previous theard crasing, or probably adding some smart [resourse limit](https://nodejs.org/api/worker_threads.html#workerresourcelimits_1)

body:
@Iamshankhadeep @sestinj 
Adding the if block from llmStreamChat to runNodeJsSlashCommand on its own doesn't work because the abort is never triggered. I think this is because ideStreamRequest never yields anything back to _streamSlashCommand (where the state.active property is checked and abort is called) until the end of the stream.

However, if we keep the check for setInactive message ideStreamRequest's handler, then the abort is sent and the streaming cancels on command! [This](https://github.com/justinmilner1/continue/compare/preview...justinmilner1:continue:editDiffTest?expand=1) works.

Note that this still doesn't work for ctrl+backspace (only works for ctrl+shift+backspace).

body: @pzaback Is there any way that we might be able to achieve what you are looking for without adding a directory to the workspace? It would help to know what sort of outcome you'll want from the recorded sessions. Perhaps better filtering capabilities for the `~/.continue/sessions` folder would accomplish the same without adding complexity?
author: sestinj

body:
The main thing I'm trying to accomplish is to save those files within a repo I'm working on in order to commit them alongside code changes as documentation of how LLMs were used in the development process (inspired by how Simon Willison generally includes links to [relevant ChatGPT sessions](https://simonwillison.net/2023/Aug/6/annotated-presentations/#chatgpt-sessions) in his tweets and blog posts). I've thought this was a good first step, with plans to follow up by adding the ability to save as rendered HTML as the session appears in the sidebar when a session is loaded, rather than just raw JSON.
I'm certainly not married to any particular directory structure, and it might be better to bring up a "Save as..." dialog than use a hard-coded path, but I guess it made more sense to me to initially default to saving them within similarly named subfolders than to copy the files to the workspace root. My related concern was about adding a button in the UI for something that perhaps not many people would care to use. As mentioned above, I'm close to finishing a closely-related idea to have an IDE config flag that when selected would result in every call to historyManager.save() to mirror the session file being saved to the active workspace (again, in `{workspace}/.continue/sessions` for now) that perhaps obviates the need for this copy option, or could be complimentary in that the "copy" button is only shown if that setting is enabled. As an optional feature disabled by default, it needn't alter the directory structure for any users who don't have any interest in using it, and as an IDE config setting it could be set per workspace, so for example I'd probably personally leave it disabled for my continue workspace or when contributing to other projects, while enabling it only for personal side projects where part of the point is "hey, look how you can build/learn faster using LLMs!" or where I think transparency is important for whatever other reason.

All that being said, I _also_ think it'd make sense to have a button when viewing history to toggle between showing history results for all sessions or just within the active workspace.

body: @justinmilner1 Part of the goal with generating a link was to give users a chance to modify the issue before it originally gets published. When you create via API, I think it just immediately creates the issue, is this how that works? I think it would be nice to have a verification flow where users don't need to fear that the model outputs something scary without a chance to review. Can you think of any kind of in between solution? I don't know if there's an API for generating drafts, or if perhaps we just need to generate a more obvious link (possibly an h1 with a link rather than the small text at the bottom, or just better messaging, like "please click here to create the issue")
author: sestinj

body:
@pzaback Good catch! Just tested and pushed up your fix to avoid using 'this'.

@sestinj I definitely agree. Feels very wrong to publish the issue without manual editing or confirmation, even if the issue is heavily labeled a draft. ...Unfortunately, github doesn't have a draft option for issues currently. 

I think two changes should be made:

![Screenshot from 2024-04-10 10-41-33](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/assets/42585006/11d14ac0-0cbe-48dd-9a16-642644a62504)

1) A 'publish' button should be added into the chat bar. Alternative could be a code lens in the generated issue.

2) The draft should be generated in a new editor, rather than in the sidebar. This way the user can edit the generated issue as they wish. 

These are fairly heavy changes but I think they're necessary for this feature to really be valuable.

Any thoughts?
author: justinmilner1
sestinj

body:
@sestinj Ah I think I understand where my confusion is coming from:

When I click on the link you provided, I am _not_ taken to a draft page - instead I'm directed to the template page. When I use the issue feature on the preview branch, it takes me to 404.
If I try to create this 'draft issue' on a repository that _I own_, I am indeed taken to a 'draft' page.

I added issue templates to my repository, and still am able to reach the draft page - so I think the ability to draft the issue is indeed about repository ownership.

Note: The api is able to create issues both on repos I own and don't own.


So what to do?:
While I wish their was a native gitlab issue draft feature, I do think the 'Publish Draft' button design is sufficient confirmation to create an actual issue, _if_ the issue is labeled 'draft' (in the title/body) _and_ a window is opened with the url for the generated draft - would you agree? 


Is it worth it?:
This is a lot of additions - however, I could see this _interactivity within chat through buttons_ being used for numerous other features. Most user-guided interaction with external APIs will need some form of confirmation/rejection.... if this is something to build we should probably have a longer discussion about this.
author: justinmilner1

body:
@justinmilner1 Oooh this explains everything, I hadn't realized that at all. A bit unfortunate, but nevertheless I think the larger point about user confirmation/input is important. I would say this is interesting enough that we should go ahead and try it. Probably the first attempt won't be the exact thing that lasts forever, but would love to experiment.

The first problem to solve is probably just how to best display a button from the markdown view, and once that is accomplished, rather than making some large refactor so that slash commands can emit buttons in a general way, it might be good to just do something that allows for this to be tested more immediately
author: sestinj

body: @sestinj Got it. I'll experiment with how the button could be displayed.
author: justinmilner1

body:
@sestinj Looks like it's very easy to _render_ a button in markdown - but it's not straightforward how the button's functionality would be initialized, or how slash commands would listen for button activity, or how we would track issue generations to button activity.

My takeaway is that it's something which could be done - and that's good to know! ...but I think it's better to wait until we have more (quantity and importance) use cases for a change this large - what do you think?

@FunkMonkey I'm going through all of the many PRs that have ended up on the back burner, and I realize now that I completely missed this. The principle I think we're coming to is that it's not best to accept "input" from other extensions. What I mean by this is that you could do something like registering a custom "slash command" or "context provider" (like [here](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/1288)), but we don't want to allow arbitrary usage of Continue resources without the user triggering them. Especially when something like OAuth is in place to allow users to access resources from an account, this could pose a potential security risk.

I'm going to close this PR because of this, but I would be curious to hear in the GH issue whether you think that there might be another way of accomplishing what you're looking to do. Hope to hear from you, and hopefully we can make something work!

body:
@justinmilner1 I really like the design of this, and appreciate the ample proof of correctness : )

One thought about how this could be simplified: instead of sending a different messageType for each possible state (setIndexingFailed, etc...), can we add a property to the IndexingProgress type, like `status: "failed" | "indexing" | "starting" | "paused"` (or something similar)? This will cut out the need for keeping track of extra variables and messages. It's the only thing I would change, and everything else looks great
author: sestinj

body:
@sestinj Thanks!

I refactored 'setIndexingFailed' as an 'indexProgress' parameter - that simplified some of the logic and reduced the number of webviewProtocol requests a bit.

I looked into integrating/simplifying other areas as well, but the most recent commit is what makes the most sense to me. 

Let me know if this is what you meant!

The most recent commit has been tested the same before.
Note: Indexing seemed to be starting up much faster than before - I could not open the sidebar before indexing began, and so couldn't verify the blue dot state.
author: justinmilner1

body:
@justinmilner1 this was perfect. I then got really excited about the direction and layered on a refactor of my own lol

Now have indexing state in a single object, so there's less to keep track of and it's easier to add state later.

I tested all the stuff you showed here and it looks perfect! Ice blue was working as well when I tried in a large enough repo for there to be time

The one thing I did change, and it might be that I misunderstood, but the globalContext storage of the indexing state was a method to save current progress so that on the next window load, it could pick up in the state it left off in. I figured that this conflicts in a way with the "starting" state, and that we always try to redo indexing on window reload anyway. Perhaps it would make sense to say "if indexing failed, don't try again even on window reload", in which case we could keep this state in localstorage

anyway...thanks for an awesome PR!

body:
Note:

```ts
const stream = (ReadableStream as any).from(response.body);

yield* stream.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream("utf-8"));
```

- `response` is not an instance of `globalThis.Response` and `response.body` is not `ReadableStream`. So we need to convert `response.body` into `ReadableStream` to use `TextDecoderStream`.
- TypeScript doesn't recognize that `ReadableStream` has `from` static method so `as any` is required.

> I believe this causes the following error:
> ReadableStream.from is not a function

I found that `ReadableStream.from()` seems to be only supported in the latest VSCode.

[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/ReadableStream/from_static) says `ReadableStream.from()` is supported Node.js v20.6.0+ and the VSCode built-in Node.js version seems to be like the bellow.

| VSCode version | Electron version | Node.js version |
|-|-|-|
| [May 2024 (version 1.90)](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_90) | 29 | 20.9.0 |
| [April 2024 (version 1.89)](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_89) | 28 | 18.18.2 (`ReadableStream.from()` is NOT available) |
| [March 2024 (version 1.88)](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_88) | 28 | 18.18.2 (`ReadableStream.from()` is NOT available) |

My only question for @sestinj is whether we should update the versions in the model selection page to default to these stable versions rather than the latest.

https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/main/gui/src/util/modelData.ts#L466-L490

> **Latest**: Points to the cutting-edge version of the model for a specified generation and variation. The underlying model is updated regularly and might be a preview version. Only exploratory testing apps and prototypes should use this alias.

body:
I think we're going to want to do something slightly different here. The biggest concern for me is that the docs indexing won't happen until main indexing has completed, which might force the user to wait some time.

The alternative that I think would be ideal is to keep a "stack" of currently running jobs. They would all run in parallel, but all updates would be attached to a certain "job id" and the last created job id would always be the one displayed in the loading bar, until it was done, at which point the job beneath it, if still progressing, would take over. On hover, it could display the full stack of current jobs.

I think this would require a) updating the IndexingProgressUpdate type to include a "jobId", b) setting that "jobId" to a random UUID at the beginning of any job and making sure that the same ID is used throughout the job, c) writing the basic "stack" logic in the IndexingProgressBar component

I'm going to close this, but the thought process here was really valuable, so thank you for making the draft

Hi @priyashpatil , apologies for the slow review.

Thanks for the contribution! This is a great addition. Only point of feedback is that @sestinj and I are a little concerned that if users have to manually run an indexing command, they might forget to do so.

Nate recently consolidated the docs logic into a single class here: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/dev/core/indexing/docs/DocsService.ts#L29

I think if we added a debounce, e.g. for "scenarios where users might have auto-save enabled", we can avoid constantly indexing without introducing an additional action for the user to take.

body:
@Patrick-Erichsen 
However, the "capability" field may subsequently be able to add other fields. I am considering the possibility of supporting uploading files from the local machine, such as uploading local company PDF documents for dialogue, similar to what OPENAI currently supports.

Therefore, it may be necessary to add an "uploadFile" field in the future. Additionally, some models support both /completion and /chat/completion, such as DeepSeek and some privately owned models by companies. However, the judgment at https://vscode.dev/github/continuedev/continue/blob/dev/core/llm/llms/OpenAI.ts#L200 is problematic. The judgment here is hard-coded and should give users the option to specify whether the model supports /chat or /completion.

As I mentioned in https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues/1793, when I use One API or some third-party interfaces, this judgment causes issues, making it impossible to use the ctrl + i and /edit commands. I am considering whether to add "capabilities.supportChat" and "capabilities.supportCompletion" to allow users to explicitly indicate the capabilities of the model, rather than hard-coding it directly in the code, which has poor support for third-party relay model APIs.

If Continue is interested in providing an interface for function calls in the future, we can also implement a "capability.supportFunctionCall" field.

Therefore, I believe it is meaningful to add a "capability" object field.

body: @FozzieHi I like the idea here, it's definitely pretty important to avoid API keys. I think it's going to be really difficult to handle all possible cases because sometimes there could also be an API key in a context provider's params. Maybe we ought to just ignore config.json for autocomplete altogether. Would you be interested in making this change?
author: sestinj
FozzieHi

body:
Hi @FozzieHi , thanks for taking the initiative on this!

You made some good points on the pros/cons of both approaches but I would probably lean towards @sestinj 's solution as well - just disabling autocomplete in the Continue folder.

The more robust/long-term solution here is likely to identify any API key in any prompt and strip it out. 

In the short run, I lean towards just disabling in the Continue folder for a few reasons:
- Not much value in autocomplete in a config file
- Easy to implement/maintain
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body:
@spew - it looks like our JS target doesn't actually support  `cause` . 

[See this comment](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/49535#issuecomment-1154793325): "The constructor overload with cause is only supported with ES2022 or later."

Our config:
```json
"target": "ES2020",
"lib": ["ES2021", ...],
```

The following config resolved the type errors for me. Going to push a commit to update to it.
```json
"target": "ES2022",
"lib": ["ES2022", ...],
```

body:
Came across this and figured I'd give a bit of feedback based on my experience working with whisper and transcription stuff over the last year-ish. First, thanks for doing this -- voice is so powerful and I can't wait til this lands in continue.

Local transcription can be tricky -- I think I saw you added gpu support, which will help performance, but generally, I can see a world in which users just want to use their openai api key to do remote transcription with the whisper api. In a lot of cases, uploading the audio to openai letting them do the transcription in the cloud ends up being faster than doing it locally, even when on a gpu on a small whisper model.

Things get much trickier with streaming transcription. What I've observed you have the same performance problems with local inference generally, but streaming degrades transcript accuracy. There is some wiggle room here -- if you chunk the audio 5 seconds at a time, you'll probably get better results than 1-2 seconds, but waiting for the initial 5 seconds to load up feels weird, and it's more expensive to do the local inference on large audio chunks. 

Personally, in a code editor context, I'd prefer to wait for a little loader icon for the transcript to come back from the openai api, and have very high accuracy than have it stream the output locally. On top of that, in most cases, especially if you have fast internet, the whole thing will probably be faster than doing local inference to transcribe.

Again, thanks for all the amazing work here.

body:
@mkummer225 I've tested this a number of times, I think it's working fairly nicely, and yet I've found myself hesitating to merge. I think the intuition for that, now that I've fully explicitly reasoned about it, is the following:
- This is a feature that will probably be used by 1% or less of users on a day-to-day basis
- It adds almost 30Mb to the package
- This adds another bit of maintenance to the build process
- The fully-local implementation is going to be prone to native module-related bugs and worse performance

My conclusion is that we'll want to wait for support for a non-local implementation before merging. I'd consider this because it wouldn't require adding more size to the bundle, and will be less of a maintenance burden, but would still be great for users that want the feature!

author: callum-gander

body:
@callum-gander thanks for offering to step up here! I would want to see the following in order to feel comfortable merging:
- There is an interface for swappable Speech-to-Text providers
- This interface is implemented by the Whisper API provider (it is my assumption that Whisper API is, if we had to choose one, the best choice, but am open to suggestions)
- It is configurable like follows:

```json
"experimental": {
  "speechToText": {
    "apiKey": "<API_KEY>"
  }
}
```

- Notice above that the swappable providers are not configurable, intentionally, as there is only one currently supported (I do not wish to take on more for now)
- No native binaries are involved (failure to load is not isolated, may cause full-on crash)
- Minimal code footprint other than a self-contained folder with interface and implementations
- No build modifications
- Because good work has been done on the local whisper provider, I think that at a minimum we should link to its existence in the history of this PR, but the required assets should go

The general point I'm getting at with all of these is I hope for this feature to require the absolute minimal maintenance (it is a very cool contribution, and will make some folks quite happy, however is quite unlikely to be prioritized by us for any amount of time in the near-to-mid-term).

Let me know what you think

body:
I can help here. I have prototype code from my projects that can stream from the web speech api and also the hosted openai whisper.

In my experience, auto-sending text after speaking is often annoying, as the STT makes mistakes with homonyms all the time and I like to correct them manually before sending. LLMs can often understand the wrong text anyway, but this will decrease accuracy.

I have a configurable delay for sending text after speaking. I usually like it at 1-2 seconds. However, I find I just turn it off most of the time and send manually.

Nate I know you are skeptical of the web speech api's quality cross platform, but I'm pretty sure it's going to be fine. Since continue is hosted in essentially a uniform chrome, it might even be the same code everywhere. (Or is the JetBrains browser significantly different?)

Using hosted Whisper works surprisingly well even though whisper isn't designed for streaming. However, the implementation I have is much more complicated, requiring WebRTC and a Python intermediary which I would have to port to TypeScript.

It's probably best to skip the old whisper API and go straight to the new openai realtime api, as models that handle audio tokens rather than going through a speech to text model first are much better at not getting fooled by homonyms and etcetera. I plan on using realtime api for my apps that do speech to speech with tool use, but haven't had a chance to start using the realtime api yet.

body:
> No build modifications

@sestinj w.r.t build modifications, this implementation uses ffmpeg (a binary) that [requires build-time modifications](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/c3d3ea457a1cb0d26c12439df09efdfc3d88c51e/extensions/vscode/scripts/prepackage.js#L474) in several places in order to ensure we can gain microphone access.

This was how I was able to get voice input in VS Code. There is [no access to any of the web speech api's](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/101621). Other implementations seem to [set up a local server](https://github.com/olefjaerestad/vscode-speech-to-text?tab=readme-ov-file#usage) and use websockets to pipe microphone input from a separate web browser tab.

The only other extension that allows for truly native + non-hacky voice input is [Microsoft's own](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode.vscode-speech) for use with their CoPilot extension. They do make available [a package](https://github.com/microsoft/node-speech) but it I was unable to get the package to install on an OSX machine (it looks like it may require installation on a Windows machine(?)). They use [.NET](https://github.com/microsoft/node-speech/blob/9fc0a5eb4650761f6d63f403a4f776a5de25e054/src/main.cc#L14) in C++ to gain microphone access

As far as I'm aware this is the only other native voice input implementation to MS's

body:
Hi, just came around here :-)

BTW: None of Whisper implementations I have seen relies on mp3, all of them use 16Khz PCM mono (wav).

1) I'm not fan of OpenAI Realtime API: It cost money and I would prefer some configuration of Continue with maximum privacy. So I even set up my own OpenAI endpoints and infrastructure.

2) You mention sherpa. You already use Transformers.js, right? Did you know there is also sherpa-onnx and faster-whisper-onnx? Did you know that Transformers.js is built on top of ONNX?

If you would update Transformers.js from v2 in your codebase to v3, you would get WebGPU support out of the box.

Here is realtime-whisper-webgpu example using Transformers.js@v3 https://huggingface.co/spaces/Xenova/realtime-whisper-webgpu ...it even works on Android mobile with Chrome. On iPhone in Safari you need some experimental configuration.

Next you have also this one coded in Rust and compiled as WASM with WebGPU support, so it works in the browser: https://github.com/FL33TW00D/whisper-turbo (online demo: https://whisper-turbo.com/ )

I'm doing quite exhausting research about speech 2 text and `sherpa` is not good because it supports only English and Chinese. Base model for Whisper is good only for English, but the main advantage of Whisper models if that there are plenty of fine-tuned models for each language, and that is how you get that extra accuracy.

So I would recommend: Okay, go with commercial Realtime API for users who want to spend money and don't care about privacy, but also think about others. Whisper has very wide variety of language models. The problem is there are so many forks that try to solve the basis of Whisper implementation that has hardcoded 30s processing loop and it gets confusing. I recommend using Whisper models, but do more research on some good real-time streaming Whisper implementation.

Also, I don't like when developers write something in a programming language and then call external OS processes like FFMPEG. It always reminds me of these "script kiddies" :-D ...wouldn't there be something better? I check the code just briefly, don't remember why FFMPEG was even there. I have javascript examples with whisper for iOS as well as Windows and they take Microphone input from the browser and perform audio conversion right there without FFMPEG.

body:
I just tried a different approach: "manage an UI-independent **handle** to the continue.dev textfield (via AT-SPI) and add the text via an external application". This way the STT application can be entirely separate (all with API and model support) while at the same time insert into ANY application and widget (talk with continue.dev, talk with editor, talk with terminal etc.).

here is the python code:
```
import pyatspi
import random

def process_object(obj):
	try:
		if not obj: return False
		component = obj.queryComponent()
		if not component:
			return False
		if not obj.role in [pyatspi.ROLE_TEXT, pyatspi.ROLE_ENTRY, pyatspi.ROLE_DOCUMENT_TEXT]:
			print(f"\t{obj.name} {obj.role}: wrong role")
			return False
		#if not component.contains(x, y, pyatspi.DESKTOP_COORDS): return False

		try:
			editable = obj.queryEditableText()
			print(f"\t{obj.name} {obj.role}: editable")
			return True
		except Exception:
			print(f"\t{obj.name} {obj.role}: not-editable")
			return False
	except Exception:
		print("error")
		return False

if __name__ == "__main__":
	registry = pyatspi.Registry
	desktop = registry.getDesktop(0)
	for app in desktop:
		if not app: continue
		#if app.name != "gedit": continue
		if app.name != "code": continue
		print("\n" + app.name)

		obj = pyatspi.findDescendant(app, lambda o: process_object(o))
		if obj:
			old = obj.queryText().getText(0, -1)
			print(f"old content: {old[0:80]}")
			editable = obj.queryEditableText()
			new = "hello world" + str(random.randint(1000, 9999))
			editable.setTextContents(new)
			print(f"text '{new}' inserted into external application '{app.name}'")
```

```
sudo apt install python3-pyatspi
python3 -m venv --system-site-packages venv
```

requires accessibility support enabled in order for vscode to provide AT-SPI information:
```
"editor.accessibilitySupport": "on"
"accessibility.signalOptions.volume": 0
```

**unfortunately** the continue.dev text input doesn't have the text role (`ROLE_INVALID`). all the standard search fields and editor panels have `ROLE_ENTRY` but cannot be edited.

**ideas**
* get a textfield into continue.dev which can be externally edited.
* make a standalone vscode extension which can at least retrieve textinput-handles within vscode (i.e. not using AT-SPI).
* just store the transcribed text into clipboard and have to user manually paste it (LobeChat background service?).

body:
@qtnx this is quite a good start! I think given our status on being able to fully take over maintenance of another extension (we want to continue focusing our internal efforts on VS Code and Jetbrains for a time), and the early stage of development that this is in, the most helpful thing I can do is help shape guidelines around contribution and the direction of work that would make us most likely to adopt this sooner.

My biggest worry is that our fast pace of development would cause this extension to need a lot of frequent changes when we either add new UI or modify how certain existing functionality works. By the time that we take on our next editor, we want the code to be in a spot that makes it feel comfortable to add 5 more.

To get there, ideally:
- We have better documentation around how the messenger protocols work
- The messenger protocols are cleaned up (higher confidence that they contain all functionality that will be needed in the future, and have clear naming)
- The core binary has better testing, a more consistent build process, documentation, and some important command line arguments, such as being able to run it over either stdin/out or TCP on any given port
- Potentially we move the core binary from using `pkg` (deprecated and doesn't support the latest versions of Node) to using Node's built-in "Single Executable Applications" ability: https://nodejs.org/api/single-executable-applications.html
- We should fully evaluate the feasibility/benefit of adhering to the LSP standard for features like autocomplete. If this would allow autocomplete to function without even needing an extension (just the server) that would be a big deal

And in general, keep an eye out for any situation where a) you find the core protocol to be awkward or missing something that you need (this is good feedback to help us solidify the API), or b) making a lot of logic/design decisions in the NeoVim client (maybe something we should discuss putting in the core or finding standard principles for, as we'll want such things for further IDEs)

Anyway, I think you're doing great work. What I like about this NeoVim client is that because it doesn't use the React `gui`, we drop the complexity of having 3 separate messengers!

body:
> Getting an error in core/indexing/embeddings/HuggingFaceTEIEmbeddingsProvider.ts after this update however

>  indexing/embeddings/HuggingFaceTEIEmbeddingsProvider.ts(12,3): error TS2610: 'maxBatchSize' is defined as an accessor in class 'BaseEmbeddingsProvider', but is overridden here in 'HuggingFaceTEIEmbeddingsProvider' as an instance property.

I realized there will be such an error yesterday. I only implemented a getter for `maxBatchSize` in `BaseEmbeddingsProvider`, while `HuggingFaceTEIEmbeddingsProvider` will modify it in its custom handling logic.

It was the first time I wrote TypeScript and I forgot to read `CONTRIBUTING.md` so I didn't test it locally. ~~Is it okay to exercise CI or I should test it locally?~~ It seems that `CONTRIBUTING.md` didn't document how to perform CI checks locally, I will follow https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/main/.github/workflows/dev_pr.yaml and https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/main/.github/workflows/ts-check.yaml

~~Do you think we should add a `_maxBatchSize` property (not sure if it can be private), modify the getter and implement a setter in the base class? That's not very elegant. Or we can just override the getter and add a private property `_maxBatchSize` in `HuggingFaceTEIEmbeddingsProvider`.~~ I choose the latter one.

~~I don't think we need a `DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, because all derived classes have the corresponding static property.~~ (Oh it seems that `HuggingFaceTEIEmbeddingsProvider` might don't have it, but maybe we should assume `maxBatchSize = 1` if `doInfoRequest` failed.)
If we really need one, I think it should be `1`. So at least it will work instead of getting an error from the API provider.

body: I've updated the IntelliJ plugin and other places too, now my question: how the former `~.continue/` directory present in maaaany places in the documentation be called from now?
author: alula

body: I skipped adding relevant logic to the Rust code as it seems to be broken and not used yet.
author: alula

body:
Hey all, apologies for the late review here. After thinking about it for a bit, we're going to stick with ~/.continue, the primary reason being that we're often fighting not software bugs, but difficulties in making sure to guide users down the right path when they are customizing Continue. Moving the relevant files to a path that will vary per user is a real opportunity for confusion.

I appreciate the work that went into this though, so if there were interest in doing something like some easter egg flag that would have the directory stored instead at the XDG path that might be fine. Yes, it would still be complex, but I figure for the handful of users that care deeply about this that might be okay

body:
Hi @sambhavnoobcoder—sorry for the delay. I'm looking into Pieces OS more and thinking that something even better than this PR might be OpenAI-compatibility so that a custom provider isn't needed. We're reaching a point where there are such a large number of LLM providers to maintain that it is likely to cause many of them to fall out of regular maintenance. The more providers can use OpenAI-compatible servers, the more stable and up-to-date support we can offer for them, and I'd strongly prefer to do this for Pieces.

Is Pieces OS OpenAI-compatible, or is this a change that could be made? I would estimate that this would require fewer lines of code within PiecesOS than it would in this current PR

body: Hi @sambhavnoobcoder, since it's been a while and I think that the OpenAI-compatibility approach would be much better, I'm going to close this PR for the time being. Happy to take another look if you have the chance to look into the OpenAI-compatible route

Hi @Yurzs! I appreciate this draft. I want to make sure we make a decision here early before you spend too much time with the changes, and as of now we are not going to be able to merge this. The biggest reason is that by formalizing our interfaces here, it's an irreversible action, and would make it much harder for us to iterate on them. At least while we're constantly updating our teams product, this would cause a lot of backward compatibility problems.

If you're looking for ways to better manage your team config, I'd love to talk more about this and hear the specific problems you're solving for! Feel free to send me an email or message on Discord and I'd love to chat about it

author: sestinj

body:
@sestinj  

I think the 'link' attribute was misused inside siderbar.js.

Let's take "getting-started" as an example.

Docusaurus reads sidebar settings and identifies the order and hierarchy between documents.
If a category has a link property, the document it points to is considered an index document for that category.

Typically, Docusaurus generates "Next" and "Previous" links in the order listed in the sidebar.

And when you give a link attribute to a category in Docusaurus, it treats the document as if it were a virtual "index.md " of that category.

As a result, Docusaur tries to find the next page of "getting-started/install" on "getting-started/index.md " but points to itself because "getting-started/install" is the current page.

After the link is removed, the "install" page is simply treated as an item in the category.
"Next page" will now correctly point to the next item in the sidebar ("getting-started/overview").

This is close but not perfect. A few shortcomings:
- Unwanted right + left margin
- New code is getting a gutter highlight from VCS styling

I think it might be a better approach to flip the insertion/deletion logic, e.g. we use a `addLineHighlighter` for deletions without actually deleting the code, and then we use the `editorComponentInlaysManager` for insertions. This would at least get around the gutter highlight issue, and be more of a true "proposed" diff since we won't actually be modifying any source code, just applying highlights.

This would require a larger refactor of the actual insertion/deletion logic though, so I'm in favor of just merging this for now.

body:
Sorry to be back and forth again on this—part of it is time zones—but I think we still need to both:
1) Give an extremely obvious/intrusive error dialog when a validation error is stopping the config from loading
and
2) Not stop the config from trying to load when we find validation errors

At least the latter is necessary when the validation errors are only "suggestion" status and not "critical". We should probably expand the `ValidationErrorMessage` type now to be an object with status and message to make sure we're doing this right
author: sestinj

body:
> 1. Give an extremely obvious/intrusive error dialog when a validation error is stopping the config from loading

I updated the GUI, I hope that's what you had in mind. I also made the continue button slightly more explicit with 'FATAL ERROR' in all caps.

> it seems like the validation errors completely stop the config from loading, and I'm not actually sure that we want this. It's still possible to use the model, but it won't reflect the changes that the user thought they made in config.json. Especially when we want to return things that are just optional suggestions, we shouldn't stop the config from loading. This might mean we have to explicitly return rather than throwing and catching

There is a distinction between fatal and non-fatal errors now. That said, all errors are set to fatal at the moment. If any of them should not be considered fatal, you can change the boolean to `false`. That's also how you can test fatal and non-fatal error handling locally.

I hope this works!

"tabAutocompleteModel": [{

body:
Hey @reosablo thanks for doing this.

edit: Changes made here: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/2632

I've been spending some time setting up text-embedding-004 and code-gecko.

It has kind of been making me think, from a ui perspective, do you think it makes more sense to have all of vertexai under one provider?

And then inside _streamChat and all of the other functions, it handles correctly based off of the model name?

That way, when you select vertexai, you can see all of the models you have as options

I have started doing the change out of curiosity, but I wanted to get a second opinion.

Edit: thinking about it even more it gets a bit weirder.

Where do things like code-gecko live? What about Gemma? They aren't technically Gemini - do they need their entire own vertexai llm object? That feels a bit weird
author: Lash-L

body: @reosablo you don't pass any credential so how I should authenticate with vertex?
author: ppsirius

body:
@Lash-L 
> do you think it makes more sense to have all of vertexai under one provider?

That sounds like a better idea. I actually tried implementing a similar approach with `OpenAIVertexAI` extending `OpenAI` for [Llama models](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/llama), but ran into some challenges.

> Where do things like code-gecko live? What about Gemma? They aren't technically Gemini - do they need their entire own vertexai llm object? That feels a bit weird

I think that the current model providers seem to handle too many functionalities. Separating them into platform adapters and model adapters could be an effective solution. This could be a large refactoring.
author: reosablo

body:
@ppsirius
Please make sure that the Google Application Default Credentials (ADC) are properly set up on your machine. You can verify this by running the command `gcloud auth print-access-token`. This should return an access token.

If you haven't already, you'll need to run `gcloud auth application-default login` to set up the ADC.

See: https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/authentication

[Edit] Partner models like Mistral models need to be enabled to use.

See: https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/mistral#:~:text=Go%20to%20one%20of%20the%20following%20Model%20Garden%20model%20cards%2C%20then%20click%20enable%3A

- Is Not Diamond OpenAI-compatible? (or at least close to this except having an array as the models parameter and a small handful of others). author: sestinj

body:
> @dragos199993 very excited to see this! A couple of quick observations:
> 
> * It looks like there is an extraneous .idea file or two in the PR
> * Is Not Diamond OpenAI-compatible? (or at least close to this except having an array as the models parameter and a small handful of others). It would be quite nice if we could use the existing logic from the OpenAI class rather than importing the separate notdiamond-continue package (which appears to have a lot of dependencies itself)
> 
> The second point would be the biggest for us—ideally we can support NotDiamond requiring no dependencies and just using fetch, and something close to OpenAI-compatibility would probably make that easiest

Likewise, @sestinj 🚀 !

I addressed the first point and fixed the conflict (the version in package.json).

Unfortunately on the second point it might be a bit more complicated and the results might be more verbose 😢
We are not fully compatible with OpenAI and we use inside `notdiamond-continue` a few langchain packages to handle the streaming for multiple providers and models.

If we do a fetch on `model-select` we only get the name of the provider + model, but that's all 😢. I could try to reduce the amount of dependencies from `notdiamond-continue` because (as the same suggests) it's specifically for the continue integration. I can make it as slim as possible, only langchain stuff to be there.

Or if you recommend a different approach, I'll gladly address it 🙏
author: dragos199993

body:
I really do appreciate the dedication to make a package just for Continue. Unfortunately with langchain included at all, we won't be able to merge. It's 3MB, which is a non-trivial amount when we have a limit for the JetBrains extension store.

I do feel that it is going to be necessary for Not Diamond to become OpenAI-compatible anyway if other tools like Continue are to integrate easily. Whatever work is being done on the client should probably be done on the server. That said, I do admit that the extent to which this feels obvious to me might also be the extent to which I am missing something about how Not Diamond is able to provide privacy-preserving routing. Is there a more fundamental limitation?
author: sestinj

body:
> I really do appreciate the dedication to make a package just for Continue. Unfortunately with langchain included at all, we won't be able to merge. It's 3MB, which is a non-trivial amount when we have a limit for the JetBrains extension store.
> 
> I do feel that it is going to be necessary for Not Diamond to become OpenAI-compatible anyway if other tools like Continue are to integrate easily. Whatever work is being done on the client should probably be done on the server. That said, I do admit that the extent to which this feels obvious to me might also be the extent to which I am missing something about how Not Diamond is able to provide privacy-preserving routing. Is there a more fundamental limitation?

Hi there @sestinj. You're correct about our privacy-focused approach to routing, and how we avoid offering proxied (server-side) invocation as a result of that.

Would it suffice for us to skip the Langchain dependency, instead relying on Continue's already-existing dependencies on OpenAI and Anthropic TS client libraries? With this approach we could still submit requests client-side via those libs, without introducing a large binary dependency which violates size limits for JetBrains extensions.

body:
wonderings:
- frequencyPenalty or presencePenalty correlate to repeatPenalty?
- For `api/generate` Not supported yet?: `context`, `images`, `system`, `template`
- template is not included in `BaseCompletionOptions` and never passed in actual api call but `template` and `promptTemplate` are in `config_schema`?
author: RomneyDa

body:
repeatPenalty should equal frequencyPenalty

It's okay not to allow images for /api/generate—we'd only use images in chat (at least for as far as I can see into future)

context I believe is just another way of passing in the context of the current chat session, which we already do by sending chat messages

system you are right to call out (though generally /api/generate should actually be incredibly rare to use over chat so this is all fairly low priority

`template` and `promptTemplates` both correspond to general properties of the `BaseLLM` class: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/b9d3ef4a77041711e3445f0f75647b3eda8da54c/core/llm/index.ts#L141-L142 and https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/b9d3ef4a77041711e3445f0f75647b3eda8da54c/core/llm/index.ts#L171-L174

`template` being the name of a template that we have pre-made, like "alpaca" or something. "promptTemplates" being customizable way to change the Edit template, though both of these are fairly legacy now that a) every provider handlers templating for us (almost) and b) people probably shouldn't really be able to come up with a better Edit prompt than we can

body:
Commit that I pushed up is primarily to move this all under a "References" nav item.

I also attempted to make the `/customize/overview` page into a category (like this https://docs.continue.dev/customize/model-providers) for the sidebar items under the `Customize` nav item, but it doesn't seem to be possible. Category sidebar items have a dropdown toggle by default that contain all of the items associated to the category, which are what's used to generate the preview cards. See the docs here: https://docusaurus.io/docs/sidebar/items#sidebar-item-category

So, we will need to either create a custom .mdx doc that imports the relevant Card component and manually map them, or just make a regular markdown page of some sort. I would opt for a simple markdown approach since creating anything custom is pretty involved in Docusaurus, e.g. https://docusaurus.community/knowledge/component-library/new/Card/

body:
@PRANJALRANA11 Thanks for taking the time to do this! This is going to be the perfect band-aid for small codebases, but I'm trying to think ahead to what happens when there is a huge codebase: with this implementation, we would walk the entire directory every time the user changes files, which is very expensive.

I'm thinking we'll need to instead have a way of storing the .gitignore and .continueignore locations, or instead just walking up the file tree from a given location to find them. This is a bit more involved, but in the meantime what you could do is use the default ignore patterns in `ignore.ts` (which include .env, etc.) here and it would solve this problem for 90% of users
author: sestinj

```

ignore.ignores(path)
```

Future will need to think about using "didChangeActiveTextEditor" for this, that could be triggered 20 times a second, can't do anything expensive here

body:
Hi, @amytimed, thanks for the PR!

Mentioned in discord
>Hi @Amy, in config.json it uses tabAutocompleteModel, which can be set to one model or an array of models. Then it converts from intermediate to final config here, and the s is added for the final type
https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/dev/core/config/load.ts
Adding the s fixed it because now it's not finding your tabAutocomplete model so it's defaulting to starcoder2:3b, which is not causing the memory issue
It's a bit confusing but the root issue seems to be that deepseek-coder:1.3b-base is somehow requesting way too much memory, or perhaps we're not sending some param that deepseekcoder needs for memory management. Might be related to this
https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/2793

author: fbricon

body:
@fbricon thanks for investigating this! I definitely agree that we are making too many requests right now. This particular approach is going to stop us from reusing requests in later completion attempts though. The code for this is a bit convoluted at the moment, but to give an idea of what I mean: say I start typing `con`, and the LLM begins to respond, and by the time I type `s`, the LLM has already streamed up to `console.`. Even though the CancellationToken will be fired, we wouldn't want to stop this request, because it is still correct, so we let it keep going in the background, and next time a completion request happens, if it still matches the stream, we keep the stream.

I kind of feel like this is tricky enough to get right that I would hesitate to make large changes until we have some basic tests for `CompletionStreamer.ts` in place
author: sestinj

body: I understand what you're trying to do but Ollama 0.4 is currently unusable in the current situation which is an absolute blocker for us. So if you have ideas/pointers to limit the scope of the changes, I'll be happy to look into it
author: fbricon

body:
@fbricon it's not the scope of the changes that was problematic (I completely agree that this is a major problem and worth a large diff to fix it). The problem was that this would regress other parts of our autocomplete, causing many more requests to be sent.

I looked more deeply into this today, and
1. I wrote tests for the services that I am trying not to break while solving the Ollama problem (this PR: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/2963)
2. I think I've figured out exactly where we need to add the cancellation (here: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/5b85cad7a9e292ca4060d8188ec60f7d4060de40/core/autocomplete/generation/GeneratorReuseManager.ts)
author: sestinj

body:
Thanks for looking into this @sestinj. I understand why you wouldn't want to cancel an older request that's in-flight and might still be valid after additional typing, but I wanted to echo Fred's comments that if you're using a local model that's anywhere near your machine's capabilities then Continue is unusable with Ollama 0.4. Multiple requests at a time are enough to push it from sluggish to thrashing badly and unresponsive, and it's much better with this PR.

I'm wondering if this is a case where behaviour should be different between local and remote models since you'd typically optimize differently? If not, then maybe it's worth leaving the first completion going as long as it _still matches current typing_ but cancel any intermediate ones? i.e. if I type `contr` rapidly then at most I'd have the initial completion on 'c' and the last one running, but not one from the o/n/t, and the first would be cancelled too if the first four letters it returned are 'cons'.
author: deboer-tim

body:
@deboer-tim The behavior you're describing when you say

> leaving the first completion going as long as it still matches current typing but cancel any intermediate ones

is exactly what we already do (unless there is a bug), except that the intermediate requests should actually never be sent at all

On one hand I recognize that we have a really big problem on our hands here and I'm open to doing some kind of partial temporary solution to solve that, but if it requires a huge refactor *and* is disabling important functionality, then it seems worthwhile to just make the full fix immediately.

I think the question is why this code here is ever sending more than one request at a time:

https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/c6f2abd9405352a5c10c6f095e4c0d985e6bbaa7/core/autocomplete/generation/CompletionStreamer.ts#L26-L36

https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/c6f2abd9405352a5c10c6f095e4c0d985e6bbaa7/core/autocomplete/generation/GeneratorReuseManager.ts#L36

because the intention is that either we are reusing the existing request (and not making a new one at all) or we are cancelling the old request and sending a new one. So the problem seems to be that we just aren't cancelling correctly. The place we attempt to cancel is here: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/c6f2abd9405352a5c10c6f095e4c0d985e6bbaa7/core/autocomplete/generation/GeneratorReuseManager.ts#L14

I'd be open to adding an abort signal that allows this to be correctly cancelled. I was under the impression that `break`ing from a response.body async generator was supposed to automatically close the connection, but definitely could be wrong since this obviously isn't working

body:
@sestinj I changed the code so now the AbortController is managed by GeneratorReuseManager.getGenerator: 
https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/2935/files#diff-b8da7c7af454cd919c720aae65118f287416d7754359b37dd5076c7580a67993R45-R46

Calling cancel() on the ListenableGenerator now aborts the signal:
https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/2935/files#diff-e41edd4c3dbe11540aa51c644ef0df0ca0922b89314f84c2550471e70ecb2d0eR19

... that is propagated to all LLM queries. So reusing the same prefix doesn't cancel the current completion request
author: fbricon

body:
> I think the question is why this code here is ever sending more than one request at a time:

because canceling the generator was not enough to cancel the http request. You really need to pass the abort signal through

We're reaching out to ask that previous contributors sign it. Could you please take a moment to sign, or if you have any questions send me a message? (either here or nate@continue.dev would work) To do so, you just need to **post a comment below with the following text:**
``` I have read the CLA Document and I hereby sign the CLA ``` ❤️ Thank you for the work you've done on Continue, and let me know if you have any suggestions on how we can make the project even better!
author: sestinj

body:
@Patrick-Erichsen 
> Need to discuss approach to teams dropdown and config profile selection
Yes we should talk about this

Currently we can show or hide known submenu items based on context, but can't dynamically load items into the submenu.

We could could achieve the current 3 config options
- Local profile
- Personal workspace
- Team profile

Approach:
- if signed in, show "Account" icon with submenu options
   - "Use local config" shows if context "continue.usingLocalConfig" is false. Clicking triggers "continue.useLocalConfig" command, which sets "continue.usingLocalConfig" to true, "continue.usingTeamConfig" to false, and "continue.usingPersonalConfig" to false
   - same approach as ^ for "Use personal workspace" and "Use Teams workspace" submenu options
   - "Sign out" option triggers sign out command
- if not signed in, show "Account" icon that triggers sign in command

But future might be more profiles so not sustainable
@sestinj

body: Binding the http requests to the IDE cancellation token was the 1st approach I used in #2935. But as @sestinj requested, and as https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/2935#issuecomment-2488927707 explains, the abort signal has to be controlled by the generator, so you can still reuse pending streaming if the prefix is compatible with previous completion requests, as to minimize requests. This is irrelevant to response caching, that you observed.
author: fbricon

body: Right! I apologize, I missed that comment. Will fix in a moment.
author: X9VoiD

body: Done. I think `AbortSignal` is outside the scope of `ListenableGenerator`'s tee-ing function and should be managed by the `GeneratorReuseManager` instead. It makes more sense this way for me.

body:
Hey @Patrick-Erichsen thanks for reporting. I did a little investigation and found some things. Good news is the theming looks really close, but I'm unsure what happened to the sidebar chat between the time I merged that PR. There seems to be a regression on master that removes all styling from the sidebar, I'm having trouble confirming on latest master.

All this PR aimed to do was properly switch based on the `Window: Auto Detect Color Scheme` property. I didn't update any other theme logic as far as which CSS was applied. 

I did a little investigation and found that there is something else going on with the built-in theming added by continue and it's reproducible by checkout out the commit before this PR and the commit after this PR was merged. My guess was the previous behavior was buggy beforehand with the built-in themes. Anyways, I had great success with these changes locally. You can see a PR here where we can continue the conversation. https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/3210

author: sestinj

body:
@sestinj Okay, I changed this because the following steps would result in an infinite loop of requests.

To elaborate further, the steps involved are as follows:
1. There is an attribute isOSREnabled in TipTapEditor, which sends a request with a messageType of `jetbrains/isOSREnabled` to the ide when it is rendered, and **registers an eventListener about `jetbrains/isOSREnabled` in the webview.**
2. The ide receives this request and processes it, after which the ide sends a response with a messageType of `jetbrains/isOSREnabled` to the web.
3. The eventListener receives the result of `jetbrains/isOSREnabled` from the ide, and executes `ideMessenger.respond` to return a request with a messageType of `jetbrains/isOSREnabled` to the ide.

Obviously, they are in an endless loop, which eventually causes page freezes, slow LLM output, and even page crashes.

Additionally, It is worth mentioning that each dialog box will request multiple repeated `jetbrains/isOSREnabled`. If there are multiple dialog boxes on the page, there will be too many unnecessary requests.

body:
I think this solution makes sense. The original reason we were manually handling copy/paste was for a specific bug with Jupyter Notebooks in VS Code web, so not overwriting any copy/paste for JetBrains shouldn't be an issue.

> I found that when the permission status is PROMPT, it doesn't give any response

Could you share what the "permission status" is here? Not familiar with what you're mentioning.

Really appreciate both this and your other JetBrains contribution though, both of these issues are great improvements.
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body:
@Patrick-Erichsen Sure, I'd be happy to explain.
The permission status refers to the permission to read the clipboard content in the current browser. It is obtained by executing `navigator.permissions.query`:
```typescript
await navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'clipboard-read' as PermissionName }) as PermissionStatus
``` 
Its value in VSC is **`granted`**, while in JCEF it is **`prompt`**. The prompt state cannot directly obtain the clipboard content, and `await navigator.clipboard.readText()`  doesn't resolve the promise, it's hung.

As can be seen from the code, `navigator.clipboard` is used to solve problems in VSC, so we can completely not use it in JetBrains.
