Hi @ruediste, thanks for the PR and for pointing this out. The answer is that `stopNCharsAfterClosingBracket` isn't what it's supposed to be, it was a hotfix and it ended up not working too well. I opened a PR with a fix to the filtering logic with an approach that is, I believe, similar to yours: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/3044/files

Where we differ is that your approach recognizes duplicated suffixes in any case, and in my case it only handles it after a closing bracket. I added [some tests](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/3044/files#diff-929bf04dcb5dfd8bc1aeb02110c8efe7c8a8c499ef739e7f882f7d792d00db48) also.

I need to figure out with @sestinj what the next steps should be and then I'll give your PR a proper review.

body:
Managed to sort out the issue with the mssql package breaking the tests
Had to add the following to the jest.config.js

```
moduleNameMapper: {
    "^(\\.{1,2}/.*)\\.js$": "$1",
    "^uuid$": "uuid", // https://stackoverflow.com/a/73626360
    '^@azure/(.*)$': '<rootDir>/node_modules/@azure/$1',
    '^mssql$': '<rootDir>/node_modules/mssql'
  },
```

body:
> @DifferentialityDevelopment thanks for figuring this out! The `moduleNameMapper` looks correct but wondering why we're getting the error in the first place
> 
> @rootedbox is the author of this package, any chance you've ran into similar issues?
> 
> ```
>  Must use import to load ES Module: /home/azamorn/continue/core/node_modules/@azure/logger/dist/browser/index.js
> 
>       at Runtime.requireModule (node_modules/jest-runtime/build/index.js:850:21)
>       at Object.<anonymous> (node_modules/@azure/identity/dist/index.js:5:16)
>       at Object.require (node_modules/tedious/src/connection.ts:12:1)
>       at Object.require (node_modules/tedious/src/tedious.ts:2:1)
>       at Object.<anonymous> (node_modules/mssql/lib/tedious/connection-pool.js:3:13)
>       at Object.<anonymous> (node_modules/mssql/lib/tedious/index.js:4:24)
>       at Object.<anonymous> (node_modules/mssql/index.js:1:120)
> ```

So as I understand the issue so far, it only ever occurs during a specific test as far as I could tell, mssql package uses tedious package which in turn uses the @azure/identity package, during the jest testing it requires instead of importing somehow somewhere in the code and that's what sets off the issue.
I'm not even entirely clear why my addition to jest.config.js made the issue go away to be brutally honest.

The AI overlord had this to say about it

> The `moduleNameMapper` in Jest config is used to handle module path mapping and resolve import/require issues, especially when dealing with ESM (ECMAScript Modules) and CommonJS mixing.
> 
> In your specific case, the error was related to mixing ESM and CommonJS modules when testing code that uses Azure SDK and MSSQL. Let's break down the relevant mappings:
> 
> ```javascript core/jest.config.js
> moduleNameMapper: {
>   // Handles .js extensions in import paths when using ESM
>   "^(\\.{1,2}/.*)\\.js$": "$1",
>   
>   // Handles the uuid package specifically
>   "^uuid$": "uuid",
>   
>   // These two are specifically handling Azure SDK and MSSQL module resolution
>   '^@azure/(.*)$': '<rootDir>/node_modules/@azure/$1',
>   '^mssql$': '<rootDir>/node_modules/mssql'
> }
> ```
> 
> The key points are:
> 
> 1. The Azure mapping (`^@azure/(.*)$`) helps Jest correctly resolve Azure SDK modules that might be using different module systems or have specific import requirements.
> 
> 2. The MSSQL mapping ensures that when your tests try to import/require the MSSQL package, Jest knows exactly where to find it and how to handle its dependencies.
> 
> 3. The `.js` extension mapping is particularly important for ESM because Node.js requires file extensions for ESM imports, but Jest's default behavior might not handle this correctly.
> 
> This configuration essentially helps Jest properly resolve module paths and handle the mixing of different module systems (ESM and CommonJS) during testing, which is what was causing your original error.

I added the delay and two icons, now with Synfig Studio, an open source 2D drawing/animation software. I did the dot, but the animation continues running in the background, so some times the dot pops up in it's large state, sometimes in it's small state. So I added a slow spinner as well. To me the spinner looks better. Just replace the `gif` files to see both versions.

Happy to adjust the icons if you have suggestions, I'm not much of a designer ...

Just recognized that I only did the delay, not the minimum display time. I'll do this later, time to call it a day.

@ruediste I'm going to close this for now—given the amount of attention we'd want to put into the UI for this in order to ship it, I just don't think we're going to be able to prioritize it in the near-term. I'm mostly trying to avoid a situation where we ship something without polishing, have a few users use it but share negative feedback, and then we have a maintenance burden we aren't able to prioritize.

If you have any thoughts to the contrary, I'm open to hearing. In the future if/when we get back to this, I'm confident this PR will still be a great reference!

body:
Hi, I would like to know the motivation for this change. This because in the past weeks I always used the /commit command by adding the file in stage, but not always I want to commit all changes. With this merge, the LLM considers all changes and I haven't found a way to pass the option for not including the unstaged changes.

I think (for my specific use case) it is easier to choose which files the LLM should consider for building the commit message.

The only useful thing I found to solve this problem is custom slash commands, but that seems a bit too invasive.

Edit: nevermind, I just found a way, just pass the "params" in the config. In the documentation is not much clear, if you want i can try to make a PR to make a better doc about it

author: RomneyDa

body:
@HD787 I'd go ahead and push your commit for the config option, can revert if needed but I think a persisted setting is the move here.

I think there's a strong case for removing most `config.ui` params and moving them to local persisted redux with a simple config UI in the more page. This might be a perfect starting case for that.

Approach:
- Add `wrapCodeBlocks` or similar to the ui slice in `gui/src/redux/slices/uiSlice`
- ensure it is persisted to local storage in the [saveSubsetFilters](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/main/gui/src/redux/store.ts#L33-L37) here 
- Add a super simple toggle switch setting in the more page that updates this value
- In the codeblock, check the redux `wrapCodeBlocks` value rather than `config.wrapCode` (remove `config.wrapCode`)

Let me know if you'd have time to give that a shot, and thanks for the initial work, this will be a great improvement

body: so trying this, it doesn't actually fix the problem. I think the issue is if the `vscode-extension:esbuild` task is running in the background from a previous invocation, vscode isn't going to start it again even if it's called for (since it's already running).  So if you have `vscode-extension:esbuild` generate extensions.js then have `vscode-extension:continue-ui:build` call `prepackage.js` which removes extensions.js, calling `vscode-extension:esbuild` again later is going to be a noop, I think, and not regenerate the file (since it's still running in the background)
